gaps.quote: So $q$ divides no numerator or denominator of the finitely many matrices used.
gaps.note: Does not follow from the previous sentence, which only requires that q not divide the denominator xi. Numerators may be divisible by q (e.g. the entry 0 = 0/1 has numerator 0). What invertibility mod q^b of F_1, F_2 actually needs is that q divide no denominator and no diagonal numerator of F_1 and F_2. The page never says why the F_1, F_2 produced by elimination satisfy this; a pivot divisible by q would put q in a denominator.

gaps.term: any invertible linear transformation costs O(V)
gaps.quote: Any invertible linear transformation of $H$ or $D$ costs $O(V)$ (cited)
gaps.note: Stated too widely. The argument that follows (update from last to first, each coordinate a combination of earlier unchanged ones) works only for lower-triangular transformations, and even then the new coordinate also uses its own old value, so it is 'itself and earlier' coordinates. A general invertible transformation, such as a permutation of the fields, is not an O(V) in-place pass; that is why interchanges are counted separately. Correct statement: any invertible lower-triangular transformation (with diagonal entries units mod q) of H or D costs O(V).

gaps.quote: The paper shows $N<2L_{\rm b}$, so $s_{\rm b}<W_{\rm b}R$.
gaps.note: With the formula s_b = W_b R - N + 2L_b, N < 2L_b gives -N + 2L_b > 0, hence s_b > W_b R, the opposite of the conclusion. To get s_b < W_b R from that formula one needs N > 2L_b. Either the inequality or the formula's sign is wrong.

gaps.quote: The network's rank budget, which counts dimension changes along its edges, gives $s_{\rm b}=W_{\rm b}R-N+2L_{\rm b}$
gaps.note: The identity is presented as following from a 'rank budget' that the page never states or derives, and it is not marked as cited. The reader cannot see how summing edge ranks yields W_b R - N + 2 L_b.

gaps.quote: $N$ the number of negative source projections
